subject: Madagascar
note: Hand-curated research for a Geographica episode about Madagascar. Claims are cited to a pinned Wikipedia revision (trusted_secondary). The map shows the island as it is today; the breakups are described, not drawn. India is a flagged country in the map data and is only labelled, not highlighted.

claims.text: Madagascar is an island country in the Indian Ocean, lying off the southeastern coast of Africa.
It is the world’s fourth-largest island and the second-largest island country.
Following the prehistoric breakup of the supercontinent Gondwana, Madagascar split from Africa during the Early Jurassic period, around 180 million years ago.
It split from the Indian subcontinent approximately 90 million years ago.
This isolation allowed native plants and animals to evolve in relative seclusion, making Madagascar a biodiversity hotspot and one of the world’s 17 megadiverse countries.
